prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: this exact transparent two-view green frog-slime character atlas. The user has accepted the creature shape and now explicitly asks for MUCH STRONGER PIXEL-ART LOOK for implementation in a 16-bit RPG.
Keep the character design, front/back poses, heavy green folded body, amber eyes, subtle grin, three bottom lobes and small golden seed in the chest exactly recognizable. Keep NO flowers and NO leaves. Do not redesign or add anything.
Re-render the illustration as authentic visibly LOW-RESOLUTION, hand-placed 16-bit sprite art: each full creature should look authored on about a 96x96 to 112x112 pixel grid and then enlarged with NEAREST-NEIGHBOR so the square blocks are clearly visible at this output size. Use a consistent coarse pixel grid, stepped diagonal contours, chunky clusters, a crisp dark 1-2 native-pixel outline, 3-4 discrete shades per material, limited ~20-24 color palette, small clean block highlights. Simplify tiny surface detail into deliberate pixel clusters while preserving facial expression and thick folds. NO smooth gradients, NO antialiasing, NO soft painting, NO blurry resizing, NO grain/noisy dither, NO vector curves. Make it visibly more pixelated and retro than the input. It must be a polished finished game sprite, not a smooth illustration with a subtle texture filter.
Production layout unchanged: wide 2:1 transparent RGBA atlas, two equal square cells. LEFT front 3/4 facing left, RIGHT genuine rear 3/4 facing right. Same scale, common baseline, generous transparent margins and center gutter, entire silhouette inside each cell. Maintain actual alpha transparency around each sprite; no checkerboard painted into image, no floor/shadow/background, text, label, watermark or border.
Output only the final two-view pixel-art atlas.
